business_scope.primary_industry_name: General Partner Management Entity for Early-Stage Technology Funds

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil law for Quebec private law; common law for federal public law and criminal law; official bilingualism in English and French at federal level, French official in Quebec
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Canada-China Foreign Investment Promotion and Protection Agreement (FIPA, in force 2014)
Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement (CETA)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Federal: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, SC 2000, c 17, as amended; Criminal Code, RSC 1985, c C-46, Part XII.2; Canada Business Corporations Act, RSC 1985, c C-44, s 21.1 (individuals with significant control); FINTRAC directives and interpretive guidance. Quebec: Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c CCQ-1991, arts 2236 et seq. (limited partnership); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1; Regulation respecting the application of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c P-44.1, r 1; Charter of the French Language, CQLR c C-11.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Certificate of Good Standing of each non-Canadian corporate UBO or general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry of the UBO's home jurisdiction (e.g., Companies House, Hong Kong Companies Registry, SAMR in China)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (where the origin is a Hague Convention member; otherwise Consular Legalization by the competent Canadian consular office)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized passport copy and proof of residential address for each individual UBO and general partner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public or competent administrative authority in the country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incumbency and register of directors/partners for corporate UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate secretary, corporate services provider, or equivalent filing agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Declaration of ultimate beneficial ownership (completed and signed by the proposed general partner)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: General partner's signing officers before a notary, or certified by a qualified legal counsel
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial act; if executed outside Canada, Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, general partners, key officers, and beneficial owners against (a) Canada's Consolidated Canadian Autonomous Sanctions List (CCASL) under the Special Economic Measures Act (SEMA), (b) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, (c) the US OFAC SDN List, (d) the EU consolidated financial sanctions list, and (e) FINTRAC's published money laundering and terrorist financing indicators. For this medium-risk venture capital GP, enhanced due diligence must include a domestic and foreign PEP determination, adverse media review, and a documented risk assessment before onboarding. Screening results must be retained for at least five years after the end of the business relationship.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Québec online portal (https://www.registraireentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate/business name must be in French, except for recognized trademarks or where a French generic term is added. Non-Latin scripts must be romanized using official transliteration (e.g., pinyin for Chinese names). A limited partnership must include 'société en commandite' or 'S.E.C.' in French, or 'Limited Partnership' or 'L.P.' in English, subject to the French-language requirements of the Charter of the French Language.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: No extension of a name reservation is available; if the reservation expires, a new name reservation must be filed. Upon name rejection, the applicant may submit a written request for reconsideration to the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the rejection notice, referencing the file number, the rejected name, and a proposed amended name. If the reconsideration is maintained, the applicant may contest the decision before the Tribunal administratif du Québec (TAQ) within 30 days of the written rejection.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: A virtual office is not acceptable for the registered office. The public enterprise register requires a real physical establishment address in Quebec where service of process may be made. For a venture capital GP that may be registered with the Autorité des marchés financiers, a virtual-only office is inconsistent with the place-of-business substance expected by the regulator and by FINTRAC if the entity is a reporting entity.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Moderate (approximately 20-25% per annum probability for a licensed GP; higher risk of unannounced inspection by AMF or FINTRAC after a compliance-risk flag).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Civil Code of Quebec (CQLR c. CCQ-1991), arts. 2186-2279, in particular arts. 2236-2244 (société en commandite); Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises (CQLR c. P-44.1), ss. 21, 26-38; Regulation respecting fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises (CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 2)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (Quebec Enterprise Registrar)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Déclaration d'immatriculation (Declaration of Registration) filed in accordance with Section 21 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None prescribed by statute. A Quebec société en commandite (limited partnership) may be registered with zero minimum paid-up capital; the capital commitments of the general and limited partners are fixed exclusively by the limited partnership agreement. No statutory escrow or bank attestation is required for registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the formation and statutory registration of the venture capital general partnership (société en commandite) under the Civil Code of Quebec be, and it hereby is, approved in all respects; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the subscription of partnership capital commitments by the General Partner and the initial Limited Partners, as set out in the executed Limited Partnership Agreement, is ratified, accepted, and adopted; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that the registered office of the Partnership be fixed at Suite 100, 1 Place Ville Marie, Montreal, Province of Quebec, and the Registraire des entreprises du Québec is hereby directed to effect the statutory declaration of registration; RESOLVED, FURTHER, that [Full Name] is appointed Managing General Partner, [Full Name] Chief Financial Officer, and [Full Name] Corporate Secretary, each to serve at the pleasure of the partners until successors are duly designated.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online portal (www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS search for the proposed partnership name ending with the mandatory legal designation 'S.E.C.' (société en commandite). File an online name reservation request with the REQ, indicating the proposed corporate designation and the intended business activities of the venture capital general partnership. Retain the certificate of reservation, which is valid for 60 days and may be renewed once upon payment of the prescribed renewal fee.
required_dossiers: Completed REQ name reservation form
NUANS search report (issued by an accredited search house)
Declaration of proposed business activities (venture capital fund management)
Payment receipt for the reservation fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or marked as confusingly similar, file a revised name proposal with a written justification of distinctiveness, or request a formal reconsideration by the REQ within 15 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of Limited Partnership Agreement and Governance Instruments
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Legal counsel in the province of Quebec (civil law notary optional unless real property is contributed)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft and execute the limited partnership agreement (contrat de société) in accordance with articles 2236-2244 CCQ. The agreement must allocate capital commitments, distributions, management authority of the general partner, and, critically, restrict limited partners from participating in the control or management of the partnership in order to preserve limited liability. Obtain a certified copy of the resolution of the general partner (or its board) approving the agreement, the appointment of the initial capital contributor, and the adoption of the registered office.
required_dossiers: Executed limited partnership agreement
Schedule of capital commitments from each partner
Certified general-partner resolution approving the agreement
Identity documents (passport or provincial ID) of partners
Restrictive covenant clause limiting limited partner management powers
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the agreement is returned or challenged, revise the management and capital clauses to comply with mandatory provisions of the Civil Code and re-execute; obtain a notarial acknowledgment where immovable property is contributed by a limited partner.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing the Declaration of Registration with the REQ
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) online filing system
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Complete and submit the statutory Declaration of Registration, prescribing the partnership name, the registered office address (which must be a real address in Quebec), the identity and domicile of each general partner, the general object of the partnership, and the names of the limited partners. Pay the prescribed filing fee by credit card or electronic funds transfer. The declaration takes effect upon acceptance by the registrar.
required_dossiers: Déclaration d'immatriculation (prescribed REQ form)
Certificate of name reservation (NUANS)
Certified copy of the executed limited partnership agreement
Proof of identity of the general partner
Original or certified copy of the general partner's corporate registration (if the GP is a legal person)
Payment of the registration fee in the amount of CAD 50 (approximately USD 37)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the declaration is queried, the REQ issues a notice of deficiency; submit the missing information or corrected declaration within 30 days. Failure to cure within the prescribed period triggers an automatic rejection; a new filing and fee will then be required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Quebec Enterprise Number (NEQ) and Attestation of Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon acceptance of the declaration, the REQ issues the 17-digit Quebec enterprise number (NEQ) and an official attestation of registration evidencing the existence of the société en commandite. Download the electronic attestation and the public extract of the register, which will be used for bank account opening, contracting, and securities registration.
required_dossiers: Electronic copy of the attestation d'immatriculation
Public extract from the register of enterprises
NEQ certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the attestation contains an error of fact, submit a request for rectification under Section 30 of the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises; the correction is retroactive if filed within two years of the original registration date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Federal Tax Identifier, AML Program, and Securities Regulator Filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) and Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the limited partnership with the CRA to obtain a business number (BN) and program accounts (payroll, GST/HST/québec sales tax, and corporate tax where applicable). File a T5013 partnership information return for the fiscal period. In parallel, assess whether the venture capital general partner entity requires registration as an exempt market dealer or investment fund manager under the Quebec Securities Act (RLRQ c. V-1.1) or whether a recognized exemption applies; initiate the AMF registration or exemption application if required by the fund's capital-raising model. Implement the statutory AML/CFT program (Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act) and appoint a compliance officer.
required_dossiers: NEQ certificate and attestation of registration
Executed limited partnership agreement and GP resolution
Canadian beneficial ownership register
AML/KYC policies and procedures manual
CRA business number application (Form RC1 or online)
AMF registration or exemption application (where applicable)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CRA or AMF rejects or queries the application, provide supplementary beneficial ownership documentation and amended governance instruments within the regulator's stated curing period; if registration delays threaten the capital call timeline, apply for a discretionary exemption order or use an interim registered adviser/managed account structure approved by the AMF.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) – Québec Securities Sector
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Registration as Exempt Market Dealer (EMD) and/or Investment Fund Manager (IFM) under the Quebec Securities Act (RLRQ c. V-1.1), or an exemption order issued by the AMF for the venture capital general partner

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category III – Exempt. Office-only tertiary financial services activity; no mandatory environmental impact assessment under the Environment Quality Act (CQLR c. Q-2) and the Regulation respecting environmental impact assessment and review (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 23), Schedule I.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial effluents or VOC emissions. Office wastewater must comply with the applicable municipal sewer bylaw (e.g., Ville de Montréal RCG 16 sewer discharge limits); general waste, confidential paper, and electronic media must be disposed of under the Regulation respecting the recovery and reclamation of residual materials (CQLR c. Q-2, r. 46) using licensed contractors.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate issued by the local fire prevention service and/or the Régie du bâtiment du Québec for commercial occupancy; structural load and occupancy permit from the municipal building authority; registration with the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) for workplace occupational health and safety; implementation of a CNESST-compliant health and safety program; workplace electrical, elevator, and emergency exit inspection clearance; commercial general liability and professional indemnity insurance in force.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) — federal income tax, GST/HST registration and Business Number (BN) administration; Revenu Québec — Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ), GST/HST collection for Quebec-based businesses under the Canada–Quebec integrated tax administration agreement, Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) coordination, and provincial payroll/health-services levies; portals: CRA Business Registration Online and My Business Account; Revenu Québec TaxNet.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign non-resident venture capital GP (organized as a Quebec limited partnership) must first obtain a CRA Business Number via Form RC1 or Business Registration Online, supplying the partnership agreement and foreign registration documents, electing partnership flow-through status, and registering for GST/HST where taxable supplies in Canada exceed CAD 30,000 or voluntarily to claim input tax credits. Concurrently, register the LP with the Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ), then open a QST account with Revenu Québec where taxable supplies in Québec exceed CAD 30,000; Quebec-established businesses file combined GST/HST–QST returns through Revenu Québec TaxNet. Non-resident GPs must designate a service representative in Quebec and provide certified translations of constitutive documents; no minimum capital requirement applies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible — The Quebec limited partnership (société en commandite) is fiscally transparent under subsection 96(1) Income Tax Act (Canada) and the Quebec Taxation Act: income, gains, losses, and credits are computed at the partnership level and allocated directly to general and limited partners, including non-resident limited partners. No entity-level federal or Quebec income tax applies; non-resident partners may be exposed to Part XIII withholding on Canadian-source partnership income under ITA s. 212(2.3). The LP is not subject to a corporate check-the-box regime.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada has no check-the-box classification election; corporate or partnership status follows legal form. Relevant statutory elections for a venture capital GP partnership include: (i) subsection 216(1) ITA election allowing a non-resident partner to compute tax on net Canadian-source partnership income rather than flat gross withholding; (ii) reasonable income-allocation agreement and guaranteed-partner-compensation substantiation under ITA s. 96(1.1); (iii) GST/HST election under ETA s. 177(1) appointing the GP as agent for a non-resident fund; (iv) GST/HST related-supply election under ETA s. 272.1 and corresponding QST close-election for supplies between the GP and its related fund vehicles; (v) partnership fiscal-period election where available under ITA s. 249.1. No hybrid mismatch elective relief exists; Canada applies anti-hybrid and foreign-accrual deeming rules independently.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (federal value-added tax) plus Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) — dual VAT-type consumption tax regimes administered by Revenu Québec (for Quebec establishments) and the CRA
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 — GST/HST: worldwide taxable supplies in Canada over the preceding four consecutive calendar quarters (ETA s. 240, small-supplier rule); QST: taxable supplies made in Quebec over the preceding four calendar quarters (QLTA ss. 415 and 417). For a VC GP, management fees charged to a Canadian-resident fund count toward the threshold; zero-rated supplies (e.g., certain services to non-resident funds) are excluded. Voluntary registration remains available to recover ITCs/ITRs on professional fees, AMF regulatory licence costs, and software subscriptions.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control (CTC) regime exists in Canada or Quebec. CRA and Revenu Québec accept paper and electronic invoices without prior validation. Mandatory invoice content for GST/HST-QST includes the supplier's legal name, BN and QST registration numbers (15/16-digit), tax rate, amount of tax, and a sequential invoice number; electronic records are admissible under ETA s. 238 and Quebec record-keeping rules. Revenu Québec's TaxNet requires electronic filing and API-based remittance of combined GST/HST-QST returns for registered Quebec businesses; no fiscal-device certification applies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated under ETA Sch. VI Part V where supplied for export, delivered to a common carrier, or physically removed from Canada within 60 days of the invoice. Services: zero-rated where supplied to a non-resident person not registered for GST/HST and the service is performed wholly outside Canada (ETA Sch. VI Part V s. 20), or where the service is a supply related to exported goods. For a Quebec GP's management, advisory, and carried-interest services to a non-resident venture fund, zero-rating requires that the fund is non-resident with no Canadian establishment, the place of supply is not in Canada under ETA Sch. IX and QLTA Sch. IX, and the GP is not acting as an agent for a Canadian establishment. Fees charged to a Canadian-resident fund or to a non-resident fund's Canadian permanent establishment are taxable at 14.975%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration — CBSA electronic Commercial Export Declaration (via Canada Border Services Assessment/CESA) or the exporter's G13 proof-of-export records (Form A8A/B13) evidencing export address, HS classification, and transaction value.

Bill of Lading / Air Waybill — carrier transport document proving goods were delivered to a common carrier in Canada and departed the country; for offshore services, service-location evidence such as employee travel records, time logs, and engagement letters showing performance entirely outside Canada.

Inward Remittance Certificate — bank transfer records (e.g., SWIFT MT103) or IRC schedule evidencing receipt of foreign-currency consideration from the non-resident fund/investor, cross-referenced to the zero-rated invoice and partnership capital-call statements.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec jointly audit zero-rated claims by VC GP partnerships, focusing on management-fee zero-rating where the fund is a tax-haven resident or services are performed partly in Canada. Missing export or offshore-service documentation triggers reassessment within the normal four-year limitation window (ETA s. 298; QLTA s. 1027), converting 0% supplies to taxable supplies at 14.975% output tax plus prescribed-rate interest and late-payment penalties up to 5% plus 1% per full month (ETA s. 280). False statements or gross negligence attract penalties of up to 25% of the net tax omitted (ETA s. 285.1; QLTA s. 1001), and knowing falsification is subject to criminal fines up to 200% of the evaded tax. Revenu Québec applies a 180-day inward-remittance audit benchmark: absent a contractual deferred-payment term, failure to repatriate consideration within 180 days of invoice raises a rebuttable presumption that the supply was made in Canada and is taxable.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (BOC) exercises monetary authority and oversees the national payment clearing and settlement systems; the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) prudentially supervises the banks through which foreign exchange settlement is executed; the Financial Transactions and Reports Analysis Centre of Canada (FINTRAC) administers the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act (PCMLTFA) for all cross-border wire and EFT reporting; in Quebec, the Autorite des marches financiers (AMF) concurrently regulates the GP's exempt-market distribution, escrow conduct, and registration obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada maintains unrestricted CAD convertibility on both current and capital accounts. There is no exchange control approval, registration, deposit, or surrender requirement for inbound LP capital commitments, capital-call wiring, foreign debt incurrence, or profit remittance. The only profit remittance hurdle is tax administration: distributions and fees to non-resident LP partners attract Part XIII non-resident withholding tax (statutory 25%, reduced under the Canada-US treaty or other applicable treaties), while the non-resident partner's allocated share of Canadian-source business income is asserted through the T5013/NR4 reporting procedure with associated Part I payment obligations. FATCA and CRS reporting applies at the GP and bank level; no FX control approval is needed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no mandatory surrender, repatriation, or conversion of export proceeds or any other foreign-currency receipts. A Canadian-resident VC GP may hold USD or any freely convertible currency in domestic or offshore accounts without central bank approval. Administrative requirements are limited to: (i) T1135 foreign-income verification reporting if aggregate specified foreign property of the GP/resident partner exceeds CAD 100,000; and (ii) FINTRAC Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) filing by the receiving bank for every cross-border wire of CAD 10,000 or more.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: National Bank of Canada (Banque Nationale du Canada)
Royal Bank of Canada (RBC Royal Bank)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium-Low as a primary treasury channel. Canada has no EU-style e-money institution licence; a foreign EMI must register as a Payment Service Provider with the Bank of Canada under the Retail Payment Activities Act and register with FINTRAC as a money service business before transacting. Registered EMIs can provide efficient euro/GBP/USD pay-outs and API treasury rails, but they cannot accept deposits of committed LP capital, are not CDIC-insured, and lack OSFI-regulated clearing membership. Feasibility rating: acceptable only for reimbursement of small operating costs and travel-related GP disbursements; not viable for capital-call escrow or distribution settlement.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote onboarding is legally permissible under PCMLTFA using an approved video-verification method, but Tier-1 Canadian banks generally require an in-person or notary-supervised video interview for non-resident-held LP structures. For this Quebec GP, the mandated practice is: the GP's Canadian-resident authorized signatory must attend an onboarding interview at the bank's Montreal or Toronto office; non-resident General Partners and LP beneficial owners holding over 25% in the aggregate will be asked for a separate video interview and must execute apostilled powers of attorney or rely on the Canadian-resident GP's delegated signing authority.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident look-through ownership exceeding 25% through multi-tiered trusts or corporate conduits.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete beneficial-ownership schedule with registry extracts from Revenu Quebec and Corporations Canada; notarized passports and address proofs for each look-through UBO; the full LP agreement and offering memorandum; CRS/FATCA self-certifications (Canadian Form NR301 or equivalent) for each LP; and source-of-wealth memoranda for investors subscribing above CAD 1 million.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source-of-funds exposure to high-risk jurisdictions or crypto-heavy investor portfolios.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Blockchain-analytics reports (Chainalysis or TRM Labs) covering any crypto-origin capital; audited trail of fiat conversion through a FINTRAC-registered crypto-dealing MSB; sanctions screening attestations (OFSI, Global Affairs Canada, EU, OFAC) for every LP; and independent accounting confirmation of the custody chain for subscription proceeds.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Persons (PEP) among domestic or foreign LPs triggering enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP/UBO declaration per bank EDD questionnaire; World-Check or Refinitiv background reports for all PEP-flagged parties; a rationale letter documenting the public-office role and source of funds; a senior-management approval memo from the bank's Montreal compliance unit; and an enhanced transaction monitoring commitment.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: No Canadian physical execution capacity for signature verification of the GP principals.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled power of attorney in favor of a Quebec-resident fund administrator; certified-true-copy passport pages endorsed by a Canadian notary; attestation clause from Canadian counsel confirming the LPA authority of the signatories; and written confirmation that the GP has retained a registered Quebec exempt-market dealer or portfolio manager for ongoing regulatory nexus.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Aggregate committed capital above the bank's internal threshold (CAD 25M+) triggering enhanced capital-source review.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed subscription agreements and capital-call notices; escrow release confirmation letters from the prior custodian; audited financial statements for the fund and unaudited interim balance sheet for the GP; and a third-party Canadian counsel legal opinion confirming the partnership waterfall and the prohibition on upstream distribution until each subscription is fully settled.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant protocol: each foreign LP instructs its bank to send an SWIFT MT103 to the Canadian accepting bank (e.g., National Bank of Canada SWIFT BNDCCAMMINT) for the benefit of the fund's capital-call escrow account. Field 50K must name the subscribing LP; field 59A must show the fund's escrow account; field 70 must quote the fund legal name, capital-call number, and LP capital-account period. Use ISO 20022 purpose-of-payment code SUBS or CPTL; for USD remittances routed through an intermediary, add the corresponding SWIFT MT202 COV cover payment. Verification: the fund administrator reconciles the unique end-to-end transaction reference (UETR) against the capital-call schedule before issuing a subscription receipt; the receiving bank files the FINTRAC EFTR for any wire of CAD 10,000 or more; the GP files the applicable T5013 and CRS/FATCA returns for the tax year.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rails: (1) urgent domestic CAD through Payments Canada's Real-Time Rail (RTR); (2) same-day domestic CAD through the Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS); (3) cross-border USD settlement through the Canadian bank's US clearing membership on Fedwire or CHIPS using SWIFT MT103; (4) commercial letters of credit issued as SWIFT MT700 under ICC UCP600 for asset-backed portfolio transactions, advised through the beneficiary's bank by MT710/MT720; (5) investor distribution wires using SWIFT MT103 direct, with SWIFT MT202 COV as the cover payment whenever an intermediary bank is required.
